new_alternative_mechanisms.name: Ultrasonic fragmentation of tissue ingrowth
new_alternative_mechanisms.core_mechanism: An intravascular ultrasonic transducer (delivered via catheter to the eShunt anchor site) emits focused 20-40 kHz ultrasound that selectively fragments fibrotic tissue ingrowth at the anchor-tissue interface. The fragmentation weakens the mechanical bond between the eShunt anchor and the dural venous sinus wall, allowing low-force snare retrieval without damaging the vessel wall.
new_alternative_mechanisms.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth / endothelialization — same problem as M3_REFINED, but using MECHANICAL VIBRATION energy instead of THERMAL energy.
new_alternative_mechanisms.physical_principle: Ultrasonic cavitation and selective tissue fragmentation at the implant-tissue interface. Established in orthopedic cement removal (US6203518B1, JP2023535810A — ultrasonic tools for PMMA cement removal in revision arthroplasty).
new_alternative_mechanisms.prior_art_saturation: MEDIUM-HIGH — Ultrasonic tools are established for orthopedic cement removal (US6203518B1 'Removal of tissue', JP2023535810A 'Orthopedic cement removal tool', JP2022502169A 'Orthopedic cement removal tools and methods'). For endovascular implant retrieval, the prior art is sparse — Lens 'ultrasonic fragmentation tissue ingrowth retrieval endovascular' = 17 hits, none directly on-target. Scopus 'ultrasonic fragmentation tissue ingrowth retrieval' = 6 hits, all off-topic.
new_alternative_mechanisms.white_space_for_eShunt: MEDIUM — Ultrasonic fragmentation is established in orthopedics but NOT in endovascular implant retrieval. Specific application to eShunt anchor-tissue interface is novel. HOWEVER, ultrasonic catheters (for thrombolysis, e.g., EKOS system) are well-established — the basic catheter-delivery mechanism is not novel.
new_alternative_mechanisms.what_would_defeat_it: (1) Evidence that ultrasonic fragmentation at the dural venous sinus would cause unacceptable endothelial damage or vibration injury to brain tissue. (2) A patent teaching ultrasonic fragmentation specifically for endovascular implant retrieval (none found in this search, but search was PARTIAL). (3) Engineering feasibility: ultrasonic transducer miniaturization to fit through a jugular-sheath catheter while delivering sufficient energy.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_advantage_over_M3_REFINED: AVOIDS the thermal injury problem (no heating, no thermal isolation needed). AVOIDS the inadvertent EM activation problem (no SMA, no sensitivity to MRI/diathermy fields).
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_disadvantage_vs_M3_REFINED: Mechanism is less specific (ultrasound affects all tissue in the field, not just the anchor). Tissue selectivity depends on careful frequency tuning.

V2_search_results.direct_relevance: LOW for endovascular implant retrieval — all hits are for orthopedic cement removal or therapeutic ultrasound.

new_alternative_mechanisms.name: Laser-ablation release (light-activated anchor debonding)
new_alternative_mechanisms.core_mechanism: A photosensitive polymer or laser-absorbing coating at the anchor-tissue interface is selectively ablated by a delivered-via-catheter fiber-optic laser (e.g., 532nm green or 1470nm near-infrared). The ablation cleaves the chemical bonds holding the anchor to the surrounding fibrotic capsule, releasing the eShunt for low-force snare retrieval.
new_alternative_mechanisms.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — same problem as M3_REFINED, but using PHOTONIC energy instead of thermal energy.
new_alternative_mechanisms.physical_principle: Photothermal or photoablation cleavage of polymer bonds at a specific wavelength. Established in transcatheter laser device art (US20260083501A1 — transcatheter laser for heart valve leaflet ablation).
new_alternative_mechanisms.prior_art_saturation: HIGH — Laser ablation of tissue is well-established (US12508073B2 Paradromics, US20260083501A1 Konstantinos Spargias, JP6590399B2). Lens 'laser ablation anchor release implant' = 7513 hits. The basic mechanism is saturated for tissue ablation; novelty would depend entirely on application to ANCHOR release for retrieval.
new_alternative_mechanisms.white_space_for_eShunt: LOW-MEDIUM — Laser catheters exist for tissue ablation but not specifically for implant-anchor release. Specific application to eShunt may be considered OBVIOUS by §103.
new_alternative_mechanisms.what_would_defeat_it: (1) Evidence that laser energy at the dural venous sinus would cause unacceptable thermal injury or photon-induced tissue damage. (2) Engineering feasibility: targeting the laser precisely at the anchor-tissue interface without damaging the vessel wall. (3) §103 obviousness — combining a known laser catheter with a known retrieval need may be considered obvious.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_advantage_over_M3_REFINED: HIGH SPECIFICITY — laser can be precisely targeted to the anchor-tissue interface (vs. SMA which heats the whole anchor). LOCALIZED — no bulk heating of surrounding tissue.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_disadvantage_vs_M3_REFINED: Requires line-of-sight optical access to the anchor (may be occluded by tissue ingrowth itself). Engineering complexity of integrating fiber-optic into retrieval catheter.

google_patents_top_hits: US12508073B2 (Paradromics — Systems for tissue layer removal)
V2_search_results.direct_relevance: MEDIUM — US20260083501A1 is for heart valve leaflet ablation; the transcatheter laser delivery mechanism is transferable but no direct teaching of implant-anchor release.

new_alternative_mechanisms.name: Electrolytic dissolution of anchor (electrochemically-triggered release)
new_alternative_mechanisms.core_mechanism: A magnesium or zinc alloy anchor element that is electrochemically dissolved on demand by applying a small DC current (delivered via catheter electrodes) to the anchor site. The current drives anodic dissolution of the biodegradable metal anchor, releasing the eShunt body for retrieval within minutes.
new_alternative_mechanisms.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — same problem as M3_REFINED, but using ELECTROCHEMICAL energy instead of thermal energy.
new_alternative_mechanisms.physical_principle: Anodic dissolution of biodegradable metals (Mg, Zn, Fe alloys) under applied potential. CN112998918A (W.L. Gore) explicitly teaches 'selectively degradable implantable devices comprising at least one region that is selectively degradable by electrolytic corrosion. Electrolytic corrosion of the medical device is initiated [by applied current]'.
new_alternative_mechanisms.prior_art_saturation: MEDIUM-HIGH — W.L. Gore CN112998918A (selectively degradable by electrolytic corrosion) is a CRITICAL near-neighbor. The mechanism is taught in the prior art. Novelty would depend entirely on (a) application to eShunt anchor for RETRIEVAL (vs general biodegradation) and (b) cerebrovascular context.
new_alternative_mechanisms.white_space_for_eShunt: LOW-MEDIUM — The basic electrolytic dissolution mechanism is taught (CN112998918A). eShunt-specific application is novel but may be §103 obvious.
new_alternative_mechanisms.what_would_defeat_it: (1) W.L. Gore CN112998918A — teaches electrolytic corrosion of implantable device for selective degradation. M8 may be directly anticipated. (2) Engineering feasibility: controlling dissolution rate and preventing hydrogen gas embolism (Mg corrosion produces H2). (3) Time to dissolution — minutes-scale retrieval may require high current density causing tissue injury.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_advantage_over_M3_REFINED: AVOIDS the thermal injury problem entirely (electrochemical, not thermal). LOCALIZED — current flows only between electrodes at the anchor site.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_disadvantage_vs_M3_REFINED: Most directly threatened by CN112998918A (W.L. Gore). Patent counsel §102/§103 opinion REQUIRED before pursuing.

google_patents_top_hits: CN112998918A (W.L. Gore — Selectively degradable implantable devices, electrolytic corrosion — CRITICAL THREAT)
US10661087B2 (Biotronik — Electrical implant with fixing device)
V2_search_results.direct_relevance: HIGH — CN112998918A directly teaches electrolytic corrosion of implantable device. This is a MAJOR prior-art threat.

new_alternative_mechanisms.name: Mechanical vibration decoupling (resonant-frequency anchor release)
new_alternative_mechanisms.core_mechanism: A piezoelectric or electromagnetic actuator delivered via catheter applies mechanical vibration at a resonant frequency specific to the anchor-tissue bond, causing mechanical decoupling (debonding) without bulk tissue damage. The vibration frequency is tuned to the mechanical resonance of the fibrotic capsule-anchor interface.
new_alternative_mechanisms.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — same problem as M3_REFINED, but using RESONANT MECHANICAL vibration instead of thermal energy.
new_alternative_mechanisms.physical_principle: Mechanical resonance-induced debonding at material interfaces. Established in industrial adhesive debonding and ultrasonic welding (reverse process). Less established in medical implant retrieval.
new_alternative_mechanisms.prior_art_saturation: LOW-MEDIUM — Lens 'mechanical vibration decoupling implant retrieval' = 174 hits, mostly off-topic (graphene, sensors, MR elastography). Scopus 'vibration decoupling implant retrieval' = 15 hits, all off-topic. Stimuli-responsive implants (AU2023270305B2) mention reversible occlusion via light stimulus but not vibration.
new_alternative_mechanisms.white_space_for_eShunt: MEDIUM-HIGH — Mechanical vibration for endovascular implant debonding is NOT directly taught in the prior art found. Novelty is plausible.
new_alternative_mechanisms.what_would_defeat_it: (1) Engineering feasibility: tuning resonant frequency to a specific anchor-tissue bond in vivo is extremely challenging (biological variability). (2) Risk of mechanical damage to vessel wall from vibration. (3) May not generate enough debonding force for densely fibrosed anchor.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_advantage_over_M3_REFINED: AVOIDS thermal injury. NO SMA — no MRI/diathermy sensitivity.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_disadvantage_vs_M3_REFINED: Lowest credibility of the new alternatives — physics is less well-established for in-vivo debonding. Requires extensive validation.

google_patents_top_hits: US12126966B2 (Cochlear — Medical device impulse force damper)
AU2023270305B2 (Stimuli-responsive implants — reversible occlusion via light)
US20240023994A1 (P Tech — Methods of securing a fastener using vibration)
V2_search_results.direct_relevance: LOW — no direct teaching of mechanical vibration for implant retrieval.

new_alternative_mechanisms.name: Pre-positioned retrieval lumen (dedicated rescue channel)
new_alternative_mechanisms.core_mechanism: The eShunt incorporates a dedicated, pre-positioned retrieval lumen (a small side-channel running along the eShunt body) through which retrieval tools (snare, laser fiber, ultrasonic transducer, chemical solvent) can be delivered DIRECTLY to the anchor site. The lumen is sealed during normal operation and accessed only at retrieval.
new_alternative_mechanisms.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — provides a DEDICATED access channel to deliver any retrieval mechanism (mechanical, thermal, chemical, photonic) to the anchor site.
new_alternative_mechanisms.physical_principle: Pre-engineered access channel for retrieval tool delivery. Established in multi-lumen catheter art.
new_alternative_mechanisms.prior_art_saturation: MEDIUM-HIGH — Multi-lumen catheters are well-established (US8628562B2 Boston Scientific delivery system, US20130173016A1 Cook Ireland ureteral stent with retrieval lumen concept). Lens 'retrieval lumen endovascular' = 921 hits including 'Alligator Retrieval Device' for intracranial coil retrieval. The basic lumen-channel concept is established; novelty would depend on integration with the eShunt as a STAND-BY retrieval channel.
new_alternative_mechanisms.white_space_for_eShunt: LOW-MEDIUM — The pre-positioned lumen concept is established in catheter/delivery device art. eShunt-specific integration may be §103 obvious.
new_alternative_mechanisms.what_would_defeat_it: (1) §103 obviousness — combining a known multi-lumen catheter with an eShunt may be considered obvious. (2) Engineering: lumen adds bulk to eShunt profile, may compromise delivery. (3) Lumen may become occluded by tissue ingrowth itself.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_advantage_over_M3_REFINED: MECHANISM-AGNOSTIC — the lumen can deliver ANY retrieval mechanism (mechanical snare, laser, ultrasound, chemical solvent). COMPLEMENTARY to M3_REFINED (could be combined).
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_disadvantage_vs_M3_REFINED: Does not solve the underlying problem of tissue-ingrowth adhesion by itself — it just provides access. Still need a retrieval mechanism at the distal end. Conceptually less novel than active mechanisms.

google_patents_top_hits: US8628562B2 (Boston Scientific — Medical device delivery system)
US9220873B2 (Covidien — Double ended intravascular medical device)
US20130173016A1 (Cook Ireland — Ureteral stent with lumen)
V2_search_results.direct_relevance: MEDIUM — multi-lumen catheters are well-established but not specifically for eShunt stand-by retrieval.

new_alternative_mechanisms.name: Hygel-expansion release (osmotic-triggered anchor debonding)
new_alternative_mechanisms.core_mechanism: A hydrogel ring positioned between the eShunt anchor and the dural venous sinus wall. On exposure to a chemical trigger (e.g., glucose bolus, pH change, or ionic strength change delivered via catheter), the hydrogel swells dramatically (5-10x volume), generating mechanical stress that debonds the anchor from the tissue ingrowth.
new_alternative_mechanisms.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — same problem as M3_REFINED, but using OSMOTIC MECHANICAL force instead of thermal energy.
new_alternative_mechanisms.physical_principle: Stimuli-responsive hydrogel swelling — well-established for drug release (Lens 'hydrogel expansion triggered release' = 7190 hits). 'Hydrogel swelling as a trigger to release biodegradable polymer microneedles in skin' demonstrates the swelling-trigger-release mechanism.
new_alternative_mechanisms.prior_art_saturation: HIGH for drug release; LOW-MEDIUM for implant anchor release. Novelty depends on application to MECHANICAL ANCHOR DEBONDING (vs drug delivery).
new_alternative_mechanisms.white_space_for_eShunt: LOW-MEDIUM — Hydrogel swelling is saturated for drug delivery applications. Anchor-release application is novel but may be §103 obvious.
new_alternative_mechanisms.what_would_defeat_it: (1) Engineering: hydrogel swelling kinetics may be too slow for clinical retrieval (minutes to hours). (2) Risk of bulk expansion causing vessel wall damage or pressure necrosis. (3) Trigger specificity — must not activate in normal physiological conditions.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_advantage_over_M3_REFINED: AVOIDS thermal injury. PASSIVE — no external energy required (just chemical trigger delivery via catheter).
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_disadvantage_vs_M3_REFINED: SLOW (hydrogels swell over minutes-hours, not seconds). DIFFICULT TO CONTROL (swelling is irreversible — if it starts, can't stop).

V2_search_results.direct_relevance: LOW — hydrogels for arthroplasty/disc replacement, not for anchor debonding for retrieval.

new_alternative_mechanisms.name: Magnetic-field-triggered release (external magnetic activation of internal anchor release)
new_alternative_mechanisms.core_mechanism: A superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticle (SPION)-loaded anchor element that releases its mechanical grip when exposed to an external alternating magnetic field (AMF). The AMF causes localized heating or mechanical vibration in the SPION-loaded element, triggering release. External field is delivered via a clinical magnetic hyperthermia system (already FDA-cleared for cancer treatment).
new_alternative_mechanisms.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — same problem as M3_REFINED, but using EXTERNAL MAGNETIC FIELD activation instead of internal electrical heating.
new_alternative_mechanisms.physical_principle: Magnetic hyperthermia of SPIONs — established for cancer treatment (Lens 'magnetic field triggered implant release' = 27,700 hits). 'Repetitive on-demand drug release by magnetic heating of iron oxide containing polymeric implants' (Lens hit) demonstrates the mechanism.
new_alternative_mechanisms.prior_art_saturation: HIGH for drug release; LOW-MEDIUM for implant anchor release. The mechanism is well-established for drug delivery; novelty depends on application to MECHANICAL ANCHOR RELEASE.
new_alternative_mechanisms.white_space_for_eShunt: LOW-MEDIUM — Magnetic triggering is saturated for drug delivery. Anchor-release application is novel but may be §103 obvious.
new_alternative_mechanisms.what_would_defeat_it: (1) ATTACH_3 risk for M3_REFINED applies HERE TOO — inadvertent activation from MRI fields is a CRITICAL concern (1.5T and 3T MRI scanners are common). (2) Magnetic field penetration to deep CSF-venous anatomy may be limited. (3) §103 obviousness — combining SPIONs with implant release is taught for drug delivery.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_advantage_over_M3_REFINED: EXTERNAL activation (no catheter-delivered energy source needed). DEEP PENETRATION (magnetic fields penetrate tissue without damage).
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_disadvantage_vs_M3_REFINED: INADVERTENT ACTIVATION from MRI is a CRITICAL safety concern (same as ATTACK_3 risk for M3_REFINED). Magnetic field localization is challenging.

google_patents_top_hits: US8900293B2 (Magnetizable object for therapeutic agent delivery — found in initial test)
V2_search_results.direct_relevance: MEDIUM for drug release; LOW for implant anchor release.

new_alternative_mechanisms.name: Cryo-debonding (cold-temperature differential contraction release)
new_alternative_mechanisms.core_mechanism: A cryo-balloon catheter delivered to the eShunt anchor site applies brief (10-30 second) extreme cold (-20°C to -40°C) to the anchor-tissue interface. Differential thermal contraction between the metal anchor and surrounding tissue causes mechanical debonding at the interface. The cryo-balloon is then withdrawn and the eShunt is snared.
new_alternative_mechanisms.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — uses COLD temperature (differential contraction) instead of HOT temperature (SMA phase transition).
new_alternative_mechanisms.physical_principle: Differential thermal contraction between dissimilar materials at low temperatures. Established in cryoablation medical devices (e.g., Endocare Cryocare) and industrial cryogenic debonding.
new_alternative_mechanisms.prior_art_saturation: MEDIUM — Cryoablation catheters are established (for cardiac ablation, tumor ablation). Specific application to implant-anchor debonding is novel. V2 search did not directly query cryo-debonding (deferred to V3 if M3_REFINED is destroyed).
new_alternative_mechanisms.white_space_for_eShunt: MEDIUM-HIGH — Cryo-debonding for implant retrieval is not directly taught. Novelty plausible.
new_alternative_mechanisms.what_would_defeat_it: (1) Engineering: tissue-adhesion strength at -40°C may not be sufficiently reduced. (2) Cryo injury to vessel wall/endothelium/dura. (3) Time to cool interface (heat sink effect from blood flow).
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_advantage_over_M3_REFINED: AVOIDS HEATING — no thermal injury to surrounding tissue (cold injury is more localized and reversible than heat injury). LOWER inadvertent-activation risk (no external EM field sensitivity).
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_disadvantage_vs_M3_REFINED: Differential contraction may not generate enough force to break fibrotic adhesion. Requires contact cryo-balloon positioning against anchor.

new_alternative_mechanisms.name: Photochemical bond cleavage (light-activated chemistry at anchor interface)
new_alternative_mechanisms.core_mechanism: A photo-cleavable linker (e.g., coumarin, nitrobenzyl, or BODIPY-based) chemically incorporated into the anchor structure. On exposure to a specific wavelength of light (typically UV 365nm or visible 405nm) delivered via catheter fiber-optic, the linker undergoes photochemical cleavage, severing the anchor from the eShunt body. The eShunt body is then snared.
new_alternative_mechanisms.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — uses PHOTOCHEMICAL bond cleavage instead of thermal SMA phase transition.
new_alternative_mechanisms.physical_principle: Photocleavable chemistry — well-established in drug delivery (photocleavable linkers for nanoparticles). Specific application to implant anchor release is novel.
new_alternative_mechanisms.prior_art_saturation: MEDIUM-HIGH for photochemistry; LOW-MEDIUM for implant anchor release.
new_alternative_mechanisms.white_space_for_eShunt: MEDIUM — Photocleavable linkers are established but not for endovascular implant release. Novelty plausible.
new_alternative_mechanisms.what_would_defeat_it: (1) UV light penetration through tissue is limited (need direct line-of-sight via catheter). (2) Photochemical cleavage kinetics may be too slow for clinical retrieval. (3) Stability of photocleavable linker over multi-year implant duration (must not degrade spontaneously).
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_advantage_over_M3_REFINED: AVOIDS heating entirely. HIGH SPECIFICITY — only the photocleavable linker is cleaved, no collateral tissue damage.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_disadvantage_vs_M3_REFINED: Engineering complexity: requires (a) stable photocleavable linker chemistry, (b) UV/visible light delivery catheter, (c) long-term in-vivo stability. UV light safety concerns.

new_alternative_mechanisms.name: Pressure-pulse shockwave decoupling (hydraulic shockwave at anchor interface)
new_alternative_mechanisms.core_mechanism: A modified lithotripsy catheter (e.g., electrohydraulic or electromagnetic shockwave generator) delivers focused hydraulic shockwaves to the anchor-tissue interface. The shockwaves cause mechanical debonding of the fibrotic capsule from the anchor, similar to how lithotripsy fragments kidney stones.
new_alternative_mechanisms.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — uses HYDRAULIC SHOCKWAVE energy instead of thermal.
new_alternative_mechanisms.physical_principle: Extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy (ESWL) — established for kidney stone fragmentation. Intravascular shockwave catheters exist for calcified plaque modification (e.g., Shockwave Intravascular Lithotripsy system, FDA-cleared).
new_alternative_mechanisms.prior_art_saturation: MEDIUM — Shockwave intravascular lithotripsy is established for calcified plaque (Shockwave Medical Inc. patents). Specific application to implant-anchor release is novel.
new_alternative_mechanisms.white_space_for_eShunt: MEDIUM — Shockwave for calcified plaque is saturated; shockwave for implant-anchor debonding is novel.
new_alternative_mechanisms.what_would_defeat_it: (1) Vessel wall damage from shockwave energy. (2) Engineering: targeting shockwave precisely at anchor-tissue interface. (3) May fragment the eShunt itself rather than just debonding it.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_advantage_over_M3_REFINED: AVOIDS heating. Established catheter technology (Shockwave Medical) — engineering risk lower than M3_REFINED.
new_alternative_mechanisms.key_disadvantage_vs_M3_REFINED: Less specific — shockwave affects all tissue in the focal zone. Risk of eShunt fragmentation rather than clean release.

ranking_for_V3_consideration.rationale: Highest combined white space + credibility + addresses M3_REFINED's two key weaknesses (thermal injury + EM activation). Ultrasonic catheter technology is mature (EKOS).
Highest engineering credibility. Could be COMPLEMENTARY to M3_REFINED rather than replacing it — provides access channel for any retrieval mechanism. Patent defensibility may be weak (§103).
Cryo-debonding inverts M3_REFINED's thermal approach (cold instead of hot). Lower inadvertent-activation risk. Engineering risk moderate. V3 search deferred.
Shockwave lithotripsy technology is mature (Shockwave Medical). Engineering risk lower than M3_REFINED. Less specific than M3_REFINED.
Novel concept but lowest credibility. Resonant frequency tuning in vivo is challenging.
High specificity but engineering complexity (photocleavable linker + fiber-optic + long-term stability).
DIRECTLY threatened by CN112998918A (W.L. Gore). Pursue ONLY if patent counsel finds §102/§103 distinction.
Laser ablation is saturated for tissue. Anchor-release application may be §103 obvious.
Hydrogel swelling is saturated for drug release. Slow kinetics. Difficult to control.
Suffers from SAME inadvertent-activation risk as M3_REFINED (ATTACK_3). Magnetic triggering is saturated for drug release.

key_insight: M6 (ultrasonic fragmentation) is the strongest alternative to M3_REFINED. It addresses both of M3_REFINED's anticipated weaknesses (thermal injury from ATTACK_2, inadvertent EM activation from ATTACK_3) by using a NON-THERMAL, NON-EM-SENSITIVE mechanism. Ultrasonic catheter technology is mature (EKOS, Ultraviolet Pharmaceuticals). The primary V2 limitation is that prior-art search was PARTIAL due to Google Patents rate-limiting — V3 should complete M6 prior-art search (PatSnap, PatentBear free web search) before committing to FEA.

implications_for_V3.if_M3_REFINED_survives_V2: V3 should run FEA on M3_REFINED AND conceptual design study on M6 in parallel. M6 is the strongest fallback if ATTACK_2 or ATTACK_3 destroys M3_REFINED.
implications_for_V3.if_M3_REFINED_destroyed_by_ATTACK_2_or_3: V3 should pivot to M6 as the new leading candidate. Execute full prior-art search (PatSnap + PatentBear free web) on M6 before any FEA.
implications_for_V3.if_M3_REFINED_destroyed_by_passage_audit: Already determined in V2 — M3_REFINED survives passage audit (no DIRECT_HIT found). Pivot to M6 if future attacks (V3 ATTACK_4, ATTACK_5) destroy M3_REFINED.

honest_negative_results: M8 (electrolytic dissolution) is directly threatened by CN112998918A (W.L. Gore) — should NOT be pursued without patent counsel opinion.
M7 (laser ablation) is saturated for tissue ablation — §103 obviousness concern.
M11 (hydrogel expansion) is saturated for drug release — §103 obviousness concern.
M12 (magnetic triggered) is saturated for drug release AND suffers from same MRI inadvertent-activation risk as M3_REFINED.
